key_factors: (a)(1) wholly obtained or produced in a single country
decisive_step: Mining of the amethyst clusters, druzys, and points at the Thunder Bay mine in Ontario, Canada
flip: Mining the raw amethyst stones in another country (such as Brazil) and shipping them to Canada solely for simple cleaning.
reasoning: The amethyst clusters, druzys, and points (classified as unworked semiprecious stones of heading 7103) are mineral products extracted directly from the Thunder Bay mine in Ontario, Canada, and only cleaned there without any foreign materials or third-country processing. Under 19 CFR 102.1(g)(1), mineral products extracted from the soil of a country are wholly obtained or produced in that country. Therefore, pursuant to 19 CFR 102.11(a)(1), the country of origin is Canada.

key_factors: (a)(1) wholly obtained or produced, or (a)(3) tariff shift to 9504.40

decisive_step: CNC machining of carbon fiber sheets and 3D printing of plastic components in Canada

decisive_step: Cutting, machining, and fabricating the wooden cabinet components from raw lumber and assembling the cabinet in Canada
flip: If the black walnut hardwood were pre-fabricated into finished furniture parts (subheading 9403.91) in the United States prior to export to Canada, failing the tariff shift and shifting the analysis to 102.11(b).
reasoning: The wooden record player stand is classified under subheading 9403.60, HTSUS (other wooden furniture). key_factors: (b) essential character of the South Korean steel pipes
decisive_step: Manufacturing and bending of the steel pipes in South Korea

reasoning: The finished automotive coolant pipe assembly and its pre-bent steel pipe components are both classified in heading 7304 (or 7306) per Note 2 to Section XV, or heading 8708. decisive_step: Flattening, trimming, shaping, resin-filling, butterfly stitching, and finishing the Thai raw wood slab and root into a dining table in Canada

In Canada, extensive woodworking (planing, cutting, resin filling, butterfly stitching) transforms the Chapter 44 wood into a subheading 9403.60 table, satisfying the tariff shift (see precedent N357951).

decisive_step: Assembly and integration of the functional modules, EOX reactors, piping, and electrical systems into the modified container in Canada

decisive_step: Melting, mixing, and molding the beeswax, hydrogenated soybean wax, and oils into prepared waxes in Canada

decisive_step: Assembly of the compressor, evaporator coil, condenser shroud assembly with blower, converter assembly, and housing into a complete truck air conditioning unit in Mexico

key_factors: (c) equal consideration of the bulk glues of Taiwan origin

key_factors: (a)(3) purification removing at least 80 percent of existing impurities under Chapter 29 Note 1 / 3204 tariff shift
decisive_step: Industrial purification and chloride reduction in Canada eliminating over 80% of existing impurities from Chinese ODB-2

Because laboratory reports confirm >80% impurity removal in Canada, Canada is the country of origin.

decisive_step: Cutting, bending, punching, welding, coating, and assembling the steel tubes and plastic components into a finished safety gate in Mexico

reasoning: As a composite good under GRI 3(b), the steel safety gate's essential character is imparted by the steel frame, classifying it as a household article of iron or steel under subheading 7323.99, HTSUS. decisive_step: Overmolding, assembly, and manufacturing of the bolt seal in Mexico

reasoning: The high-security container bolt seal is classified under subheading 8309.90, HTSUS (seals and other packing accessories of base metal), as the steel pin, bushing, and locking ring provide the essential locking function under GRI 3(b). Under 19 CFR 102.20(o), the tariff shift rule for headings 8309-8310 requires a change from any other heading. Foreign steel and plastic materials from outside heading 8309 undergo injection overmolding and assembly in the USMCA country (Mexico), satisfying 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3) (analogous to N364328).

decisive_step: Injection molding of US-origin polypropylene resin into plastic archival containers in Canada
flip: If the containers were molded in the United States and merely assembled, inspected, or packaged in Canada, the origin would be the United States.
reasoning: The plastic archival containers are classified in subheading 3926.90.9989. Under 19 CFR 102.11(a)(3) and 102.20(g) (as cited in N357063 and N352810), the required tariff shift for heading 3926 is a change to heading 3922 through 3926 from any other subheading, including another heading within that group. The US-origin polypropylene resin (heading 3902) is injection molded into finished containers of heading 3926 in Canada, satisfying the required tariff shift and conferring Canadian origin.

key_factors: (a)(3) tariff shift to 4202.12 (Scenarios 1-3) and (b) essential character of the molded plastic shells (Scenario 4)
